visual_observations.issue: The foreground hull does not rock once on the calm water; instead, the entire ship moves forward and to the right, creating a wake. The ship also has numerous stick figures on deck that were not present in the reference image.
The five British ships do not hold in a broad staggered line; the foreground ship moves significantly.
The camera is not locked; it subtly zooms in and pans right.
The scene is not a closer crop of the nearest existing bow and the same shore beyond; it is a completely different shot with a different ship and different background elements.
Other fleet vessels disappear from the harbour; the second shot shows only one ship.
The camera is not locked; it subtly zooms in and pans right.

The sky, golden cloud shapes, clear air, calm water, and intact shore silhouettes do not remain identical from first to last frame. The sky and water color change, and the shore is different in the second shot.
The animation does not maintain the 'exactly five British ships' inventory throughout; the second shot only shows one ship.

The style of the ships and the background elements in the second shot do not match the 'drawn stick figures with round off-white heads, dot eyes, thin limbs, bold dark contours and drawn period backgrounds' style consistently. The ship in the second shot has a more detailed, less 'stick figure' appearance, and the people on board are not stick figures.

audio.heard: A loud, sustained, low-frequency rumble with a metallic clang, followed by a distinct 'whoosh' sound, then silence.

events.description: Loud, sustained, low-frequency rumble with a metallic clang

observations.summary: The animation fails to match the visual and audio instructions significantly. The ships do not behave as described, the camera is not locked, the number of ships changes, and the second shot is a completely different scene. The audio contains a loud, sustained rumble and a whoosh, which is not a 'short hull creak or water slap' followed by silence.
